chunks: 1. Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jayyid al-Qummi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Fadalah, from Jamil, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام described to us the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. He called for a vessel of water, then put his right hand into it and took a handful of water and let it flow over his face from the top of the face. Then he wiped both sides with his right hand. Then he returned the left hand into the vessel and let it flow over the right arm, then wiped its sides. Then he returned the right hand into the vessel, then poured it over the left arm, and did with it as he had done with the right. Then he wiped his head and his feet with the remaining moisture in his hands, and did not return them into the vessel.
2. And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said:

I performed wudu (ablution) for Abu Ja'far عليه السلام at al-Jam', and he had urinated. So I handed him water and he performed istinja'. Then I poured for him a handful, with which he washed his face, and a handful with which he washed his right forearm, and a handful with which he washed his left forearm. Then he wiped his head and his feet with the remaining moisture.
3. As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: Is it permissible for a man to wipe his feet with the moisture remaining from his head? He indicated with his head: No. I said: With new water? He indicated with his head: Yes.
4. And what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about wiping the head. I said: Should I wipe my head with the moisture in my hands? He said: No. Rather, you place your hand in the water and then wipe.

The way to understand these two reports is that they are to be carried upon a mode of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of many of the 'ammah. It is also possible that what is meant by them is when the limbs of taharah have dried due to negligence on his part, so he needs to renew washing them; then he takes new water, and that taking for them is a taking for wiping, according to what the first report contains. As for the second report, it is possible that what is meant by his saying, “Rather, place your hand in the water,” is the water that remained in his beard or eyebrows, and there is nothing in it to indicate that he should put his hand into the water that is in the vessel or elsewhere. If that is considered possible, then it does not conflict with what we have already presented of the reports.

5. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Wahb, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from one who informed him, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man forgets to wipe his head while he is in salat (prayer). He said: If there is moisture in his beard, then let him wipe with it. I said: What if he has no beard? He said: He wipes from his eyebrows or from the eyelashes of his eyes.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah, dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain conditions
key_terms.النَّدَى: moisture, the residual wetness used for wiping
key_terms.بِلَّةِ: remaining moisture, the wetness left in the hands after washing
key_terms.حَاجِبَيْهِ: his eyebrows, another place from which moisture may be taken
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard, from which remaining moisture may be taken
key_terms.مَسَحَ: wiped, referring to passing moisture over the head and feet
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described

ai.seo_question: Can the head and feet in wudu be wiped with the remaining moisture of the hands, or is new water required?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the manner of wudu (ablution), especially washing the face and arms and wiping the head and feet with the remaining moisture in the hands. It also presents reports that seem to suggest using new water, then reconciles them by explaining them through taqiyyah or by interpreting them as referring to remaining moisture in the beard or eyebrows rather than fresh water from the vessel.
